thread:
raj: incident-bot just paged me — GPU decode nodes are seeing repeated CUDA OOMs during streaming, lots of request drops. stack traces attached in logs. urgent? :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Pager: severity=sev2, service=serve-runtime, runbook=decode-oom-streaming, page_id=PD12345
mel: seeing the same, dashboard spike at 02:12 UTC, decode queue backing up, error rate 23% for /v1/stream.
jorge: logs from node gpu-rt-09: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at decode_kernel.cu:421` followed by container crash (exit 137) and kube restart. repeating thrice.
raj: any recent deploys?
deploy-bot: deploy finished: service=serve-runtime image=redwood/serve:release-2026-03-15-8a3f, rollout 02:05 UTC (canary->stable).
mel: 02:05 aligns. but older nodes also show similar errors before rollout window. maybe workload changed: client A sending huge max_tokens=20000 in streaming requests.
kim-cs: Customer ticket #9872 reports partial responses and dropped streams starting 02:10. They posted their prompt/headers — they set max_tokens to 0 unknowingly and a client-side loop caused runaway generation.
raj: ok mitigation plan: 1) temporarily enforce per-request token cap at the ingress (10k) 2) route affected traffic to fallback model small-ram-quantized 3) cordon & drain the flapping nodes 4) contact customer 5) track error budget.
mel: doing 1) now — updating edge policy: `limit: max_tokens=10000, fail_mode=reject` 
mel: applied. rate of OOM errors dropped from 23% -> 9% in 60s.
jorge: starting step 2) create routing rule to divert requests with mem-heavy flags to small-ram-quantized. patch: `route: if request.seq_est > 8k -> model: small-ram-quantized`
deploy-bot: route change submitted, activating in region us-west-2 in 30s.
infra-oncall: cordoning gpu-rt-09/10 now. `kubectl cordon gpu-rt-09` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-rt-09`
infra-oncall: drain started, but several pods stuck terminating — seeing attach/detach timeout to NVMe. possible kernel-level hang after OOM.
raj: if kernel hang, escalate to infra team to reboot nodes. we need replacement capacity first.
mel: scaling up spare pool: `replicas: +4` on dedicated-gpu-pool, new nodes requested (gpu.c6.large) — ETA 3m.
kim-cs: Customer #9872 confirms they unintentionally hit a loop; they asked for an ETA on fix and whether data was truncated.
raj: message CS: we're throttling token caps and routing to a lower-memory model; no persisted data lost, partial responses may have been dropped. will follow up when stable.
jorge: also found decode process hitting KV-cache growth — persistent KV growth with repeated prefix churn from open stream sessions. adding a safeguard to kill decode if per-request KV > 6GB. patch posted to runtime: `if kv_cache_bytes > 6e9: abort_generation("kv-growth")`
mel: that patch compiled and rolled to canary nodes. no observable regressions.
infra-oncall: gpu-rt-09 rebooting now (soft reboot timed out). watching node rejoin.
raj: while we replace, enable fallback policy: if node becomes unhealthy -> model variant fallback to reduce memory usage. set fallback window = 30s.
mel: fallback policy live. error rate trending down to 3% after fallbacks and routing.
deploy-bot: stable rollout of canary hotpatch (kv-growth abort) completed at 02:34 UTC.
kim-cs: relaying to customer: we've applied throttles and fallbacks; would you be able to reduce client-side max_tokens to <5k while we stabilize? they answered yes and turned on client-side limiter.
jorge: we still saw one container crash with `cuda driver lost` before reboot — probably GPU driver got wedged. adding node label `gpu-wedged` to avoid scheduling while investigating.
infra-oncall: node gpu-rt-09 marked `gpu-wedged`, support ticket raised with cloud vendor. collecting dmesg: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:...): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus`
raj: that Xid 79 is consistent with non-recoverable GPU fault. escalate to hardware ops and vendor.
kim-cs: customer updated: they saw improved success rate after client change but asked for root cause.
mel: root cause hypothesis: combination of runaway generation from client + KV cache growth + a wedged GPU driver causing decode to exhaust memory catastrophically.
raj: next steps: 1) keep token cap & routing for 24h 2) add server-side per-session KV lifetime eviction for long-running streams 3) vendor RMA for wedged GPU node 4) retro + postmortem to refine runbook and add automatic header-based sanity checks.
jorge: opened incident in status page, set ETA for full remediation in 8h. created follow-up ticket to add a pre-filter that rejects absurd max_tokens and warns customers.
mel: adding automated test for kv-growth to our test harness so we can catch regressions on memory-hungry patterns.
raj: thanks all. handing off to infra-oncall for reboot follow-up and to mel for runtime patch monitoring. oncall rotation: @infra-oncall you're up for next 4h, @mel you own runtime until stable.
infra-oncall: acknowledged — will monitor node health and vendor comms.
incident-bot: Incident updated: incident_id=INC-2026-03-389, severity=sev2, status=mitigated->monitoring, owner=mel, oncall=infra-oncall
kim-cs: I updated the customer ticket and CS playbook. tagging legal/compliance for any follow-ups.
raj: quick note for retro: add explicit behavior for `max_tokens=0` (client bug) to be treated as invalid input. and ensure ingress rejects obviously malicious token loop patterns.
mel: agreed. will draft retro doc and add to postmortems folder.
jorge: final: no additional customer data exposed, no persistence corruption. metrics to watch: decode error rate, restarted container count, kv_cache_bytes distribution.
raj: closing thread for now, will reopen if error rate rises above 5% again. thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
